```{python}
#| label: fig-lna-block
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Block diagram of an LNA. Typically, the LNA input is impedance matched to 50 Ω, while the output is often not matched if the LNA is integrated on-chip. Often, the LNA gain is adjustable (shown with the arrow) to allow for gain control in the receiver depending on the signal conditions. The LNA also might have a low-power bypass mode to reduce the power consumption of the LNA for sufficiently strong signals." 
import schemdraw as sd
import schemdraw.elements as elm
import schemdraw.dsp as dsp

sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=2, fontsize=14, margin=0.5)

    dsp.Line().right(d.unit/2).label(r'$\text{RF}_\mathrm{in}$', 'left').idot(open=True)
    amp = dsp.Amp()
    dsp.Line().right(d.unit/2).label(r'$\text{RF}_\mathrm{out}$', 'right').dot(open=True)

    # Adjustable-gain arrow across the amp (dashed = optional feature)
    cx = (amp.input[0] + amp.out[0]) / 2
    cy = (amp.input[1] + amp.out[1]) / 2
    elm.Arrow().at((cx - 0.6, cy - 0.6)) \
        .to((cx + 0.6, cy + 0.6)) \
        .linestyle('--')
```
